questions.q: What is the real SQL syntax for declaring an incrementally-processed pipeline table?
options: CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE ... AS SELECT ...
DECLARE STREAMING TABLE ...
INSERT INTO STREAMING TABLE ...
CREATE TEMP TABLE ... AS SELECT ...
questions.explain: CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE, reading from a source like cloud_files(), is the real syntax for a streaming table in a pipeline.

questions.q: In the gold_daily_revenue materialized view example, how is its dependency on bronze_trips actually declared?
options: By an ordinary FROM bronze_trips reference in the SELECT query — no special syntax
By listing it in a separate dependencies.yaml file
By a DEPENDS ON bronze_trips clause
Dependencies must be declared manually in the pipeline UI
questions.explain: A plain table reference is the entire dependency declaration; Lakeflow infers execution order from it automatically.

questions.q: In the current pyspark.pipelines Python API, how does one pipeline function reference another table's output?
options: An ordinary spark.read.table() or spark.readStream.table() call
Tables cannot reference each other in Python
By importing the other function directly
A special dlt.read() call that must always be used
questions.explain: The current dp module uses ordinary Spark read calls; the older dlt module required a special dlt.read()/dlt.read_stream() call.

questions.q: Why did Databricks & Delta Lake Lessons 50-52 only show the Python side of pipeline syntax?
options: Because SQL syntax for pipelines did not exist at the time
Because that course taught PySpark from scratch, and Python was the more natural fit for its own progression
Because materialized views only work in Python
Because SQL cannot express dependency inference
questions.explain: SQL is just as complete a surface as Python for pipelines — the earlier course's choice was about its own teaching progression, not a capability gap.

questions.q: What's the key difference between @dp.table and @dp.materialized_view?
options: @dp.materialized_view cannot depend on any other table
@dp.table only works in SQL, never in Python
@dp.table is used with a streaming read; @dp.materialized_view is used with a batch read
There is no difference — they are interchangeable in every case
questions.explain: The choice between the two decorators depends on whether the underlying read is a streaming read or a batch read.
